html:
The war of 1516 and 1517 in which the Ottoman sultan Selim I destroyed the Mamluk Sultanate and took Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz.

Selim had just beaten the Safavids of Iran at Chaldiran in 1514, and the Mamluks stood between him and the Arab lands. In August 1516 his army, strong in cannon and musket, met the Mamluk cavalry at Marj Dabiq north of Aleppo. Sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri died on the field, and Syria fell almost without a fight. In January 1517 Selim won again at Ridaniya outside Cairo. The last Mamluk sultan, Tuman Bay II, fought on in the streets and was hanged at one of Cairo's gates.

The war changed what the Ottoman state was. Its lands, once on the edge of the Islamic world in Anatolia and the Balkans, now held Damascus, Cairo, and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, whose protector the sultan became. Egypt's grain and taxes fed Istanbul for three centuries. Mamluk households did not vanish: they ran Egypt's politics under Ottoman governors until Muhammad Ali killed their leaders in 1811.
sum: The war of 1516 and 1517 in which the Ottoman sultan Selim I destroyed the Mamluk Sultanate and took Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz.
